name: Boron

lead: Boron is a trace element found in fruit, vegetables, nuts and legumes and is sold as a supplement, typically as boric acid, calcium fructoborate or boron citrate. It is not classed as an essential nutrient in humans, although it is considered beneficial.

In bone-focused circles it is used for its possible effects on mineral and sex-hormone metabolism. Human evidence is limited to small studies, and it should not be taken to enhance facial bone structure.

paras: Proposed effects include influencing the metabolism of calcium, magnesium and vitamin D, and modulating steroid hormone levels and inflammatory markers. The exact mechanisms in humans are not well established.

Normal food intake is safe, but high supplemental doses can cause nausea, diarrhoea and other toxicity, and an upper intake level has been set by authorities. Concerns include reproductive and developmental effects at high exposures, so it should be avoided in pregnancy without advice.
